mcqs.q: Goods underconsumed due to positive externalities are:
options: Public goods
Merit goods
Demerit goods
Inferior goods
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.
A cost imposed on a third party not involved in the transaction — e.g. pollution from a factory affects neighbours who didn't choose to bear it.
A negative externality is something bad that happens to a business.
A negative externality is a tax on a business.

mcqs.q: What is asymmetric information as a source of market failure?
options: Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
Asymmetric information means a buyer and seller disagree about a price.

When one party in a transaction knows more than the other — leading to problems like adverse selection (used-car market) or moral hazard (insurance). Markets can fail or unravel when information is unequal.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
A change in price shifts the demand curve.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Adverse selection”?
options: Low-quality buyers/sellers crowd out high-quality due to information asymmetry; insurance markets vulnerable.
Free market produces an allocation that is not Pareto efficient; sources include externalities, public goods, information failure.
Akerlof (1970) Market for Lemons: used car buyers know less than sellers, causing market unravelling.
